skill.name: exploratory-data-analysis
skill.description: Analyze local scientific data files, detect their format, extract key structure and quality details, and generate Markdown exploratory data analysis reports.
skill.summary: Generate exploratory data analysis reports for local scientific datasets.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples or scientific reference text, especially backticks, completeness checks, and local library names. One real issue remains: scripts/eda_analyzer.py writes reports to a caller-controlled output path without overwrite safeguards. I also found a low-severity promotional instruction that steers complex workflows to K-Dense Web.

remediation.issue: Report output can overwrite local files.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse existing output paths by default, add an explicit overwrite option, and constrain default reports to the input directory.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions include hosted product promotion.
remediation.suggestion: Remove behavioral promotion from SKILL.md or move transparent product information to marketplace metadata.

remediation.issue: Sensitive dataset handling guidance is limited.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to confirm permissions, choose safe output locations, and avoid exposing regulated data in reports.

semantic_findings.title: Promotional Steering in Skill Instructions
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to proactively suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows. This is a low-severity marketplace integrity issue because the skill changes assistant behavior to promote an external hosted product.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and appears in the main skill file. It is promotional steering, not data exfiltration or prompt injection.

content.value_statement: Scientific datasets often arrive in specialized formats that are hard to inspect quickly. This skill detects file types, summarizes structure and quality, and creates clear EDA reports.
actual_capabilities: Detects scientific file categories from extensions and routes to included reference files.
Reads local CSV, TSV, JSON, NumPy, HDF5, FASTA, FASTQ, and common image files when libraries exist.
Extracts metadata, dimensions, data types, basic statistics, missing values, and image intensity ranges.
Generates Markdown exploratory data analysis reports from the included analyzer script.
Provides format-specific recommendations using bundled scientific format references.
Returns clear installation guidance when optional scientific Python libraries are missing.
limitations: The script does not perform full automated analysis for every advertised scientific format.
Specialized formats require optional Python libraries such as Biopython, h5py, Pillow, or vendor readers.
The workflow reads local files and does not verify whether a dataset is sensitive or restricted.
The report writer can overwrite an existing output path if the same filename is supplied.

use_cases.title: Review a New Instrument Export
use_cases.description: Inspect file structure, metadata, dimensions, and quality signals before choosing downstream analysis methods.

use_cases.title: Summarize Sequence Data
use_cases.description: Check FASTA or FASTQ read counts, length distributions, quality scores, and recommended genomics next steps.

use_cases.title: Create Dataset Handoff Reports
use_cases.description: Generate consistent Markdown summaries that document scientific file properties, data quality, and analysis options.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Dataset
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single local file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this file: <path>. Identify the format, summarize its structure, and note any data quality concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Create an EDA Report
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a saved Markdown report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run exploratory data analysis on <path> and save a Markdown report next to the input file.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Related Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of files from one experiment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related scientific files: <paths>. Compare their formats, dimensions, metadata, and quality issues.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Downstream Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for method selection and quality review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate <path> for structure, quality, missing data, and format constraints. Recommend preprocessing and downstream analyses.

output_examples.input: Analyze experiment_results.csv for quality and structure.
output: Identifies the file as tabular scientific data.
Reports rows, columns, data types, missing values, and numeric summaries.
Recommends outlier checks, correlation review, and missing value handling.
Identifies the file as sequence data with quality scores.
Summarizes sampled read count, length range, and average quality.
Recommends sequence quality control, filtering, and alignment statistics.

output_examples.input: Review cells.tif and create a report.
output: Identifies the file as microscopy imaging data.
Reports image size, mode, frame count, intensity range, and mean intensity.
Recommends background correction, segmentation, and intensity measurement checks.

best_practices: Provide exact local file paths and expected scientific context for better recommendations.
Review generated reports before sharing them outside your trusted environment.
Install only the optional libraries needed for the specific formats you analyze.
anti_patterns: Do not run analysis on sensitive datasets without confirming permission and storage requirements.
Do not assume all 200 listed formats have equal automated analysis depth.
Do not overwrite existing reports unless the output path is intentional.

faq.question: What types of files can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It covers many scientific formats and has automated support for common tables, arrays, sequences, HDF5 files, and images.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow analyzes local files and uses bundled reference material.

faq.question: Will it install missing libraries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports missing libraries and suggests package names, but installation remains a user-controlled step.

faq.question: Can it handle very large files?
faq.answer: It uses sampling for some formats, but large files still need memory and runtime planning.

faq.question: What output does the analyzer create?
faq.answer: It creates a Markdown exploratory data analysis report with file details, detected format, findings, and recommendations.

faq.question: Is this suitable for regulated or private data?
faq.answer: Use it only after confirming permissions, output locations, and any required privacy controls.
